meeting_header:
Date: 2027-09-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Mia Chen (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (CTO, Pelagos), Priya Menon (ML Lead), Sam Brooks (Infra), Dana Li (PM)
Recording: https://redwood-recordings.example/meetings/pl-20270908-1087
summary: Intro discovery to understand Pelagos Labs' model selection needs across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Key topics: required context length (8k vs 32k+), multilingual support (EU locales), tool-calling/function calling for retrieval and internal tools, security (VPC/KMS/SOC2), and benchmarks. Agreement to run a 3-model pilot on Pelagos sample prompts; Redwood to send pricing and security docs.
topics: Context window requirements and tradeoffs (8k vs 32k)
Open model comparisons and quantization impact
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Security: VPC, KMS, SOC 2, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan P: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. Uh this is Jordan from Redwood, with Mia on the SE side. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Alex R: Good, thanks. Busy week but, uh ready to dig in.
[00:12] Mia C: Hey all. We'll keep it pragmatic — goal is to figure out model selection and deployment mode that meets Pelagos's latency, cost, and security constraints.
[00:20] Dana L: Thanks. We're mainly evaluating options for chat and doc-summarization workflows, and some code gen.
[00:28] Jordan P: Great. Quick agenda — 1) use cases and SLAs, 2) context window and multilingual needs, 3) tool-calling + retrieval, 4) hosted vs dedicated vs private, 5) next steps. Sound good?
[00:35] Priya M: Yep. We'll start with context — we have long documents, sometimes 20k tokens, but we try to chunk. Ideally we'd like 32k support for multi-doc summarization.
[00:45] Mia C: Okay 32k is a common ask. Tradeoffs: bigger windows can increase memory and cost; some open models support 32k natively but perf and latency vary. We usually recommend testing 8k first unless the UX requires full 32k.
[00:59] Sam B: Our infra constraint — we prefer Private or Dedicated because of data residency and VPC peering. But cost is a factor.
[01:07] Jordan P: Totally. We can map workloads to deployment modes. Hosted is fastest to get going with our hosted API; Dedicated gives reserved GPU capacity and predictable throughput; Private gives full control for on-prem/VPC with KMS integration.
[01:20] Alex R: On models — Priya mentioned wanting open models. Which ones are you benchmarking?
[01:25] Mia C: We typically benchmark a few: Mistral and base Llama-like family, Mistral-7B-instruct variants, Llama-2 / Llama-3 variants, and some newer open 8k/32k models like Orca/Redwood-verified community forks. Also, Replicate and Cohere were discussed earlier — but we'll focus on open-weight models for Private deployments.
[01:42] Priya M: Important: we need strong multilingual support — English, French, German, Spanish. Benchmarks should include EN+EU locales.
[01:48] Mia C: We'll include multi-ling testsets. Note: some quantized weights degrade multilingual quality, so we'll track that.
[01:55] Jordan P: On tool calling — you mentioned retrieval + internal APIs?
[02:00] Dana L: Right. We need the model to call an internal tool to pull user account metadata and sometimes trigger a codegen pipeline. Security around tool outputs is key.
[02:08] Mia C: Redwood supports function/tool calling patterns and you can restrict tool surfaces. For Dedicated/Private, you can run the tool connector inside the VPC. For Hosted, we provide secure connector patterns with token scoping.
[02:22] Alex R: Any gotchas with streaming and tool-calls at larger context windows?
[02:27] Mia C: Streaming with large context is fine but latency can be impacted by kernel selection and KV cache behavior. We have continuous batching and KV cache to mitigate repeated prefixes. We'll test with your real prompts.
[02:41] Priya M: We care about deterministic output for summarization — are there model recommendations for that?
[02:46] Mia C: Determinism often comes down to sampling settings, temperature, and model family. Some instruction-tuned models are more stable. We'll include deterministic runs in the bench.
[02:55] Jordan P: Let's talk numbers — what latency targets do you need?
[03:00] Alex R: For end-user chat, p95 under 600ms ideally. For batch summarization, p95 under 4s is acceptable.
[03:07] Mia C: p95 under 600ms on open models is ambitious on high context lengths. With Dedicated and optimized kernels you can get closer; also using smaller tuned model variants for chat and larger ones for summarization is a common pattern.
[03:21] Sam B: On security, SOC 2 and KMS are must-haves. Also need audit logs and RBAC.
[03:27] Jordan P: Redwood has SOC 2 and can integrate with customer KMS/HSM in Dedicated/Private options; audit logs per request are available in the Console. We'll send the security pack.
[03:38] Priya M: Data residency — we host EU data in EU regions; need to confirm certificate for that.
[03:44] Mia C: We'll confirm region options and whether Private on-prem is required. For many customers, Dedicated in an EU region suffices.
[03:52] Jordan P: On cost — what's your budget or cost sensitivity?
[03:55] Alex R: We're early stage but cost matters. Want to compare per-token costs across models and deployment modes.
[04:01] Mia C: We'll provide indicative per-token plus infra amortized estimates for Dedicated and Private. Also, batching and prefix cache reduce per-token cost; we'll model that for your workload.
[04:12] Priya M: Can you run quantized weights? We're concerned about latency and cost.
[04:16] Mia C: Yes, quantized models (8-bit/4-bit) are supported in our runtime; but quality varies. We'll include quantized runs and call out any quality regressions.
[04:26] Jordan P: Let's capture success criteria — what would make this a win for Pelagos?
[04:30] Dana L: Accurate EU language summaries at or above our baseline, p95 latency targets met, and clear security posture. Also, easy rollout plan from proof-of-concept to Prod.
[04:39] Priya M: Also need tool-calling reliability for internal APIs and rate limiting.
[04:43] Alex R: And cost not exceeding X — we'll share ballpark numbers offline.
[04:49] Mia C: Great. Pilot suggestion: Redwood runs 3-model pilot (one smaller fast model, one mid-sized instruction-tuned, one large long-context) against your 50 sample prompts in EN + FR + DE. We'll measure quality, latency, and cost.
[05:00] Priya M: That sounds good. For tooling, how do we connect our retrieval layer?
[05:05] Mia C: For Hosted we offer a secure connector pattern; for Dedicated/Private, you can run a sidecar retriever in your VPC and call the runtime over private networking. We'll include diagrams.
[05:16] Alex R: Any limit on concurrent tool calls?
[05:20] Mia C: Limits depend on capacity; Dedicated gives reserved GPUs and you can set autoscale policies. Hosted has rate limits but higher tiers increase capacity.
[05:30] Jordan P: A couple of clarifying q's — do you need model explainability or hallucination tracking?
[05:36] Priya M: We'll need hallucination metrics for summarization; ideally a flagging pipeline.
[05:40] Mia C: Redwood Console can emit per-route quality metrics and integrate with eval sets. We can set up regression alerts keyed to your prompt sets.
[05:51] Alex R: For multilingual, can we do fine-tuning or instruction-tuning?
[05:56] Mia C: For now we recommend prompt engineering + retrieved context; for advanced needs, we support model fine-tuning depending on license of the base model — Private gives the most flexibility.
[06:07] Dana L: About timelines — we want a pilot within 2–3 weeks. Is that feasible?
[06:11] Jordan P: Yes, if you can share samples this week. We'll provision pilot instances and Mia will run the bench.
[06:18] Priya M: Ok we'll try to share samples by Friday.
[06:22] Sam B: On network — we need VPC peering and private endpoints for Dedicated. What's involved?
[06:27] Mia C: We'll provide a VPC peering guide; Dedicated supports private endpoints and we can do a security review to confirm. For Private on-prem we ship a package.
[06:38] Alex R: A quick question about model fallbacks — if a large long-context model is busy, can you degrade to a smaller one?
[06:44] Mia C: Yes, smart routing and fallback policies are supported — you can set policy by latency or cost and allow redirect to compatible variants.
[06:54] Jordan P: Any objections or constraints we haven't heard?
[06:57] Priya M: Just regulatory — some customers will insist on no cross-border data; may require Private in specific cases.
[07:05] Jordan P: Understood. We'll call that out in the deployment plan.
[07:10] Mia C: For the pilot, we'll run three models across your sample prompts. We'll capture p50/p95 latencies, token counts, and quality metrics (ROUGE / human blind eval for summaries).
[07:20] Dana L: How will we score tool-calling reliability?
[07:24] Mia C: We'll measure success rate of tool response, error rates, and end-to-end latency including retrieval.
[07:31] Alex R: On pricing — will you send per-hour and per-token estimates?
[07:35] Jordan P: Yes — we'll send a concise price sheet: hosted per-token, dedicated reserved price bands, and private licensing.
[07:42] Priya M: One thought — for chat latency, maybe use a smaller tuned model on the path and the bigger long-context for batch summary.
[07:49] Mia C: Exactly — hybrid approach reduces cost while preserving quality where needed.
[07:55] Sam B: About KMS integration — we need to use our HSM, not Redwood KMS. Is that possible?
[07:59] Jordan P: For Dedicated/Private, yes we integrate customer-managed KMS/HSM. Hosted can support bring-your-key patterns for certain tiers; we'll clarify in security docs.
[08:10] Priya M: Will you include examples of quantization impact?
[08:13] Mia C: Yes — bench will have FP16 baseline and then 8-bit/4-bit quant results with quality deltas.
[08:21] Dana L: Any limitations around function-calling when models are quantized?
[08:25] Mia C: Function-calling itself is orthogonal, but some quantized weights show subtle tokenization drift that can affect prompt parsers; we'll check.
[08:37] Jordan P: Are there any compliance reviewers on your side when we send security docs?
[08:40] Alex R: Sam and our security lead will review. We may request an NDA before some deeper artifacts.
[08:46] Jordan P: Noted — we can handle NDA paperwork.
[08:50] Priya M: For the pilot success criteria — can you put it in writing?
[08:54] Jordan P: Yes, we'll propose an acceptance matrix: quality thresholds per language, p95 latency caps, and tool-call reliability percentage.
[09:03] Mia C: I'm going to note some assumptions for the bench — will use your real prompts, run deterministic settings for summaries, and track human eval for a subset.
[09:13] Alex R: Sounds good. A couple of smaller items: any RBAC controls for who can hit which model?
[09:19] Mia C: Console supports token-level access controls and route-level RBAC. We'll include screenshots.
[09:25] Dana L: Ok. What's the timeline again for deliverables?
[09:29] Jordan P: Jordan sends pricing + security pack by 9/10; Pelagos shares prompts by 9/15; Mia runs bench and shares results by 9/17; follow-up deep-dive week of 9/20.
[09:39] Priya M: Confirmed.
[09:41] Jordan P: Any final questions?
[09:43] Alex R: No, thanks for the clarity.
[09:45] Mia C: Great — we'll follow up with a short summary email and the attachments.
[09:50] Jordan P: Thanks everyone. Meeting adjourned.
[46:50] End of recording: stated duration ~47 minutes
notes: AE+SE pair present (Jordan + Mia) — common pattern
Customer leaning Dedicated/Private due to data residency but open to Hosted pilot
Pilot: 3-model runs with multilingual tests and quantized comparisons
